record.original_question: If Γ is the permutation on words over {a,b} defined in the source, must cycles containing odd-length words have odd length, cycles containing even-length words with an odd number of a letters have even length, and cycles containing even-length words with an even number of a letters be allowed to have either parity?

evidence.quote: The cycles of Γ containing words of odd lengths are also of odd lengths. Those containing words of even lengths, with an odd number of occurrences of a, are also of even lengths. Those containing words of even lengths, with an even number of occurrences of a, may have either odd or even length.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the binary alphabet $\{a,b\}$ and the set $\{a,b\}^*$ of all finite words on this alphabet. For each word $w$ associate a non-crossing partition by the following factorization: write $w = w_0\, c_1\, w_1\, c_2\, w_2 \cdots c_k\, w_k$ where the letters $c_i$ are matched in the unique non-crossing way that pairs each $a$ with a $b$ to its right (when possible), and let $\Gamma$ be the permutation on $\{a,b\}^*$ induced by cyclically rotating this factorization (so that $\Gamma$ preserves the length of $w$ and the number of occurrences of each letter; in particular $\Gamma$ restricts to a permutation $\Gamma_n$ on words with $n$ occurrences of $a$ and $n+1$ occurrences of $b$, and more generally to a permutation on each class of words of fixed length $\ell$ and fixed number of $a$'s).

Prove or disprove each of the following statements about the cycle structure of $\Gamma$:

(i) Every cycle of $\Gamma$ that contains a word of odd length has odd length.

(ii) Every cycle of $\Gamma$ that contains a word of even length whose number of occurrences of $a$ is odd has even length.

(iii) Cycles of $\Gamma$ containing words of even length with an even number of occurrences of $a$ may have either odd or even length (i.e., both parities actually occur).
artifact.status_search_result: A related result of Castronuovo, Cori and Labbé (WORDS 2017 proceedings) establishes that the permutation $\Gamma_n$ on words with $n$ letters $a$ and $n+1$ letters $b$ has all cycles of odd length. The broader cycle-parity statement covering all length/letter-count classes appears in the WORDS open-problems list, and no published resolution of this generalized conjecture was found in the available sources, so its current status is not clearly determined.

status_evidence.title: A Permutation on Words in a Two Letter Alphabet
status_evidence.snippet: A permutation Γₙ is defined on the set of words with n occurrences of a and n+1 occurrences of b. All cycles of this permutation are of odd lengths.
status_evidence.claim: The odd-cycle-length result is established in the special case of words with n a's and n+1 b's.

status_evidence.title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures (arXiv:1705.04055)
status_evidence.snippet: In connection to the development of the field of Combinatorics on Words, we present a list of open problems and conjectures that were stated during the ten last meetings WORDS.
status_evidence.claim: The parity-of-cycles statement is part of an open problems compilation from the WORDS conferences.
